rights_note: Supplied by the project owner for this project's own use as a likeness. The card shows a cut of the portrait with a stand-in label burned on; the full pictures are kept in the evidence repository. Pixels of the turnaround sheet's four views of the head are baked into assets/humans/web/likeness/pa1904_grey_mrs_w_l_skin.jpg, which is served from the site as the figure's skin, hair and eyes (the owner, 2026-11-13: "i want them photographic matched"); of the smiling photograph only the opening of the mouth (the upper teeth, 64 x 160 pixels of that sheet) is baked into it, and the shape of the smile is fitted to it; no label can be burned on a skin, so the stand-in label is on the person's card.

access_notes: Read by eye at full size and at 3x on the face. The file carries no capture or software metadata (EXIF: orientation and 72 dpi only), so where and when the picture was made cannot be read from it. asset_use is texture, not geometry: a tier-5 picture is not evidence of anyone's outline (docs/PROVENANCE.md). The model's face is fitted to it, and the turnaround sheet's pictures are laid on that face as its skin, only because the owner chose them as the stand-in likeness; face and skin are liberties graded reconstructed (docs/LIBERTIES.md, L-prairie-likenesses-3547 and L-grey-photograph-skin-3553), not a measurement or a picture of the person. The sheet carries no capture metadata either, and was read by eye at full size. The smiling photograph was read by eye at full size, levelled by 34.2 degrees: a real photograph taken close to and from a little below, in open shade, so its light and its lens are not the sheet's (the face is laid on the fitted one before it is used, and only the teeth's colour, brought to the sheet's light, comes from it).
note: THIS IS NOT A PHOTOGRAPH OF SARAH GREY. No photograph of Sarah Grey has been found (the household record's portrait search, docs/RESEARCH/prairie-portraits-3546). The owner chose this picture as the stand-in for Sarah Grey's face, hair and dress, as the Glessner household's stand-ins were chosen (T-3478). A sepia cabinet-style portrait, three-quarter length: a woman of middle age seated in an upholstered armchair before a painted studio backdrop of foliage, her hair drawn up from the face all round to a knot on the crown, small hoop earrings, a high lace collar fastened with a cameo brooch, and a dark lustrous day dress with a pin-tucked bodice, a row of covered buttons and full leg-of-mutton sleeves, a ring on her left hand. Her face is near-frontal, turned a little to her right, both eyes showing; about 89 px between the pupils.
